lesson_title: Piles, Buckets, Journeys: Every Graph in 60 Seconds
hook_text: Bar? Histogram? Line? Pie? One 5-second test picks the right graph every time.
clip_script: Every dataset is one of three animals. Piles: separate groups — 45 colas, 30 oranges — nothing in between, so a bar graph with gaps. Buckets: marks scooped into nought to 9, 10 to 19, rim to rim on a number line — so a histogram, bars touching, because a gap would claim marks nobody could have. Journeys: the till checked every day — 380, 420, 150, 460, 510 — so a line graph, footsteps joined in order. And the pie? Not a fourth animal — the piles squashed into one tart, already sliced; you only read it. Name the animal, and the graph chooses itself.
visual_style: Claymation-style piles of cans, buckets snapping rim to rim, a dotted footpath across a calendar, then everything squashing into a spinning pie chart.
pacing: Three quick animal reveals with visual punchlines, calm one-line rule to close.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to draw graphs that markers cannot fault.
